_comment: Evidence registry. Source of truth for which prompts have been EXECUTED, as opposed to structurally reviewed. Add an entry only when a run happened and left a record; scripts/evidence_report.py validates every identifier against the catalog and every path against the filesystem, then generates _meta/evidence-levels.md.

_fields.identifier: prompt identifier, must exist in the catalog
_fields.title: human title
_fields.evaluator: who ran it, and whether they wrote the prompt
_fields.scope: what the run covered, in one line
_fields.result: outcome in one line, including defects found
_fields.limitations: what this run does not show

evaluations.title: Systematic Debugging
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: one synthetic fixture with a hidden mutable-default defect and a green test suite
evaluations.result: protocol completed end to end; three real prompt weaknesses found and fixed in v1.2.0
evaluations.limitations: single small fixture, author-evaluated, deterministic defect, familiar stack

evaluations.title: Conversational Debugging
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: tabletop walkthrough of a constructed fixture: a nightly sync failing with 'database is locked' at commit(), where the pasted code is innocent and a second uncommitted connection in unseen code holds the lock
evaluations.result: three real prompt defects found and fixed in v1.1.0: no instruction to find other holders of the same resource, a ledger unable to record findings outside the paste, and no rule for contradictions between the user's account and the evidence
evaluations.limitations: tabletop by the author, not a live user session; single fixture; database errors name their resource, which makes this lesson unusually easy to teach

evaluations.title: Chat Select: choosing the right prompt inside a conversation
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded)
evaluations.scope: six situations routed with the prompt as written, then each routing card scored against the generated TASKS.md index as external ground truth
evaluations.result: 4 of 6 cards named the prompt that TASKS.md assigns to the situation's task; two prompt defects found and fixed in v1.1.0 (no rule for a symptom that the index files under a different heading, and no requirement that the falsifier separate two prompts within a task), plus one index defect (background jobs were not reachable from the broken-now task)
evaluations.limitations: tabletop at a keyboard by the author, who wrote the situations and the questions; no live model and no second evaluator, so it tests the instrument and not compliance with it; six situations are a smoke test, not a benchmark

evaluations.title: Chat Code Review: reviewing a paste, with the limits stated
evaluations.evaluator: the prompt's author (conflict of interest recorded, and twice over: the target file was also written by the author)
evaluations.scope: one real file, scripts/check_prompt_contract.py, reviewed as written with the 'is this safe to merge' intent; the file computes a number the repository publishes
evaluations.result: six findings, two of them defects that inflated the library's own integration metric - a stem match satisfying a filename link, and substring matches such as 'planning' satisfying PLAN.md; 30 of 157 links had been scored as named on that basis. Prompt defects fixed in v1.1.0: no rule that a published number is the correctness question, and no rule to ask about the standard as well as the framework
evaluations.limitations: author-evaluated on both sides; one small Python file whose window happened to be complete, so the window claim was not tested; no second reader
